set.n: The Iwers brothers' hidden fortune (found), homestead in Inland Township near Sunbury
set.pl: Homestead farmstead in the SE quarter of sec. 35 T80N R1W, Inland Township, Cedar County
pinev: 1885 Cedar County atlas shows the family land over the east part of sec. 35 T80N R1W with a house dot in the SE quarter; the 1930s Iowa aerial shows the farmstead there; a 1936 newspaper gives the homestead as the SE quarter of sec. 35 (about 150 m).
set.st: Bachelor brothers John, Henry and William Iwers hid their money on their 800-plus acres in Inland Township. After Henry died on 30 May 1936, iron boxes with about $112,600 in gold coin, gold and silver certificates and securities were dug from under the machine shed of the homestead, partly gold coins wrapped in newspaper in a sack; more was hidden in the house. In late July 1936 the last $21,000 the court was looking for turned up as municipal bonds in a tobacco container in a gunny sack under an old Mitchell car. Estate put at $213,500-$350,000.
set.t: FOUND: the known money was all recovered by July 1936; only strays are possible. Homestead quarter; private: ask permission.
src: AP, Cedar Rapids Gazette, 5 Jul 1936, p. 25

set.n: F. Marion Ogle's hidden gold, shanty-and-dugout farm near Medora
set.pl: Centre of sec. 9 T74N R24W, the heart of the 1940 Ogle family land just east of Medora, Warren County
pinev: Section level: centre of sec. 9 T74N R24W (BLM PLSS), the core of the Ogle family land on the 1940 Warren County farm atlas; Marion's own 1907 farm is not yet on a plat (about 800 m).
set.st: F. Marion Ogle, an unmarried Warren County recluse, lived in a small shanty and dugout on his farm. His mules bolted near the cemetery south of Indianola on 8 July 1907 and he died on 17 July without regaining consciousness. A few days before the accident he had brought $10,000 he had hidden about the farm to an Indianola bank. His estate was put at $50,000-80,000 (land, Colorado farms, bank stock), and people believed more gold was still hidden on the farm.
set.t: Two separate accounts. Becomes B once the Ogle forty (shanty and dugout) is found on a 1900s Warren County plat near Medora. Private: ask permission.
src: Des Moines Register, 19 Jul 1907, p. 2 (Indianola special)
